Question
========
`geom_bar()` (and `geom_col()`) in ggplot2 accept a `position` argument that controls how overlapping bars are arranged. Which of the following statements about its possible values are correct?

Answerlist
----------
* `position = "stack"` (the default) stacks the bars for each group on top of one another.
* `position = "dodge"` places the bars for each group side by side instead of stacking them.
* `position = "fill"` stacks the bars and additionally rescales each stack to the same total height, so the bars show proportions instead of absolute counts.
* `position = "jitter"` is the recommended way to prevent bars in a bar chart from overlapping.


Solution
========
`"stack"`, `"dodge"` and `"fill"` are indeed three of the standard position adjustments for `geom_bar()`: stacking bars on top of each other, placing them side by side, or stacking and rescaling them to show proportions instead of counts. `"jitter"`, however, is not really relevant for bar charts - it adds small random noise to point positions to prevent overplotting in scatterplots, which is not the kind of overlap bars have in the first place.

Answerlist
----------
* True
* True
* True
* False
